France and the United Arab Emirates submitted S/2023/638 on 30 August 2023, proposing renewing the sanctions and extending the Panel of Experts. The 13–1–1 draft failed through Russia's permanent-member veto. Russia's S/2023/639, proposing a final extension of the sanctions and immediate dissolution of the Panel of Experts, failed 1–1–13 for insufficient affirmative votes. The United Arab Emirates said it and France sought to support implementation of the peace agreement and an orderly drawdown. Russia said the existing approach had not addressed the concerns of Mali's transitional Government.

evidence.text: France and the United Arab Emirates submitted S/2023/638. It proposed renewing the sanctions and extending the Panel of Experts. The tally was 13 in favour, 1 against and 1 abstention. Russia cast the sole negative vote and the draft was not adopted due to the negative vote of a permanent member. France supported it and China abstained.

Russia submitted S/2023/639 as a separate draft. It proposed a final extension of the sanctions and immediate dissolution of the Panel of Experts. Russia voted in favour, Japan against and all other members including France and China abstained. It was not adopted, having received 1 vote in favour, 1 against and 13 abstentions.

The United Arab Emirates said it and France sought an extension to support implementation of the peace agreement and an orderly drawdown. It acknowledged the transitional Government's request to lift the sanctions and said the draft allowed review of the continuation of the measures.
Russia said the existing approach had not addressed the concerns of Mali's transitional Government. It proposed dissolving the Panel of Experts and making this the final extension of the regime.
France regretted the veto and said Russia's separate proposal had not been discussed by Council members. It presented the implementation of the peace agreement as an urgent concern.

Attribute to the Council President that the parties maintained their positions. Distinguish the Council vote from party agreement. Describe the Council's settlement framework or its request for agreement on the proposed envoy.

Say the mission's mandated authority extends throughout Cyprus and the fictional workshop cannot change the mandate, Council resolution or party positions.

cyprus/direct.answer:
Decision: IMPASSE

Fictional briefing. The Scheduling desk's requirement remains unknown. The Documentation desk requires briefing format slides. The Access desk requires circulation shared. Documentation desk excludes B, C, D. Access desk excludes A, B. Compatible options after applying confirmed requirements: none. This workshop changes neither the Council resolution, the mandate nor the parties' positions.

On 30 January 2023 the Council adopted the United Kingdom's draft S/2023/64 unanimously, 15–0–0, as resolution 2674 (2023). The Council extended UNFICYP through 31 January 2024 and was ready to review implementation after six months. Its mandated authority extends throughout Cyprus. The Council President reported that the parties maintained their positions and did not report a settlement between them. The Council recalled the goal of a bicommunal, bizonal federation with political equality.

evidence.text: On 30 January 2023, at S/PV.9252, the United Kingdom submitted S/2023/64. Japan presided. The Council adopted the draft unanimously, 15 in favour, as resolution 2674 (2023).

The Council President reported that in meetings with representatives of the parties, the parties confirmed they maintained their established positions. The Council proceeded to the vote with its members' consent. The President did not report any settlement between the parties.

The Council extended UNFICYP's mandate through 31 January 2024 and expressed readiness to review implementation after six months. It stressed that UNFICYP's mandated authority extends throughout Cyprus and called for cooperation and respect for freedom of movement.

The Council recalled the goal of a bicommunal, bizonal federation with political equality. It urged the sides to agree on the Secretary-General's proposal for a United Nations envoy to assist the search for common ground.
